Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres — Nxeon hosting platform), a real git repo. Standing rule: NEVER build/run dev servers/run `npm run build` in the live prod tree `/opt/nxeon` or the shared staging tree `/opt/nxeon-staging` — a past agent clobbering `.next` there broke production. Start by creating your own isolated worktree:
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-registrar-leaks -b feature/registrar-leak-fixes
cd /opt/nxeon-wip-registrar-leaks && npm install
```
Do ALL reading, editing, building, and testing inside `/opt/nxeon-wip-registrar-leaks` from that point on.

CONTEXT: There is an approved implementation plan at `/root/.claude/plans/validated-napping-possum.md` for eventually adding Namecheap and Enom as additional domain registrars alongside name.com, with the hard requirement that a registrar's identity must NEVER be visible to a signed-in customer (only in admin views). Read that ENTIRE plan file first for full context. Phase 1 of that plan (consolidating 3 duplicate name.com HTTP clients into one, in `lib/registrar.ts`) has already shipped to production — you'll see that consolidated shape already in place. You are implementing Phase 5 of that plan ONLY — closing the confirmed customer-facing "name.com" leak surface. Do NOT build the Namecheap/Enom clients themselves, do NOT build the `RegistrarClient` abstraction interface (Phase 2) — this task is scoped strictly to the leak fixes, which are valuable and shippable regardless of whether a second registrar ever gets added.

Also worth knowing before you start: there is a separate, unrelated standing rule about NEVER saying "our provider" or implying Nxeon depends on a third party for its infrastructure in any customer-facing text — Nxeon must always speak as the owner of its own stack. This applies directly to the copy you'll be writing in this task: don't just swap "name.com" for "our registrar" or "our registrar partner" — that still implies a third party exists. Use fully neutral, ownership-voiced phrasing instead (e.g. "your domain's DNS", "the registry", generic descriptions of what's happening, or just naming the feature itself — "DNS", "nameservers", "URL forwarding" — without attributing it to any external party at all, own or unnamed).

## The 8 confirmed leaks (from a completed audit — re-verify each still applies before fixing, the codebase has moved since the audit)

1. `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx` — nameserver label literally "Default (name.com)".
2. `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx` — a badge reading "name.com DNS".
3. `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx` — "name.com" badge + "moves DNS off name.com's servers" copy.
4. `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx` — "live via name.com" / "name.com URL forwarding" copy (multiple instances).
5. `lib/actions-domains.ts` — a customer-facing error string says "(name.com API keys missing)".
6. **Biggest leak vector**: every `nc()`-style HTTP helper (now consolidated into `lib/registrar.ts` after Phase 1) throws `` `name.com: ${msg}` ``, and catch sites across `lib/actions-domains.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts` pass that raw message straight through as `{error: ...}` into customer components — so any registrar-side failure (a real production incident: "name.com: Payment failed" was shown verbatim to a customer) leaks the registrar's name and raw internal error text.
7. `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`'s `setWhoisPrivacy()` returns a customer-facing note interpolating `` `WHOIS privacy at ${domain.registrar}...` `` — direct leak of the DB column value.
8. `lib/kb-tools.ts`'s `describeService()` includes `` `Registrar: ${domain.registrar}` `` in context fed to the AI live-chat assistant (mounted for signed-in customers) — the registrar name is available for the LLM to potentially echo back in a chat answer.

## What to build

**A. Static UI copy (leaks #1–4)**: fix each hardcoded string. Since there's no second registrar yet and the "never imply a third party" rule applies, don't introduce a "neutral label constant" that still says something like "our registrar partner" — just rewrite each in registrar-agnostic terms describing the actual feature (e.g. "Default nameservers" instead of "Default (name.com)", "DNS" instead of "name.com DNS", "moves DNS off Nxeon's default nameservers" instead of naming a vendor, "URL forwarding" instead of "name.com URL forwarding"). Use your judgment on exact wording per component — the goal is that nothing names or implies any external registrar, named or unnamed.

Add a standing regression test (this repo's existing pattern: plain `node:test` files under `test/*.test.ts`, run via `npm test`) that reads the source of `components/customer/**` and `app/dashboard/**` (excluding `app/admin/**`, which is allowed to show this) and fails if it finds the literal strings `"name.com"`, `"namecheap"`, or `"enom"` (case-insensitive) anywhere. This is meant to catch future regressions, not just today's instances — make sure it would actually fail against the ORIGINAL (pre-fix) code, then confirm it passes after your fixes.

**B. The structural fix for dynamic leaks (#5–8, the higher-value half of this task)**: introduce a `RegistrarError` class (put it in `lib/registrar.ts`, since that's the file with the actual HTTP boundary post-Phase-1-consolidation) that every registrar HTTP failure throws, carrying:
- `registrarId` (a string identifier — hardcode `"namecom"` for now, it's the only one)
- `rawMessage` (the original, full, registrar-attributed error text — for server-side logging/audit only, NEVER shown to a customer)
- `customerMessage` (a generic, pattern-matched, registrar-name-free string safe to show a customer)

Design `customerMessage` by pattern-matching known failure categories from the raw message (e.g. anything mentioning "payment"/"balance"/"insufficient" → something like "We couldn't complete this right now — no charge was made. Please try again or contact support."; anything else → a generic fallback like "Something went wrong on our end completing this request. No charge was made if this was a payment action; please try again or contact support."). Be honest in the fallback copy — don't claim "no charge was made" for actions that aren't payments (e.g. a DNS update) — tailor the generic fallback per call site if that distinction matters, or keep it error-scope-neutral ("please try again or contact support") when it's ambiguous.

Update every catch site currently doing `{error: errMsg(e)}` or interpolating a raw registrar message into a customer-facing string (across `lib/actions-domains.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts`, `lib/actions-domains-transfer.ts`) to check `e instanceof RegistrarError` and use `e.customerMessage` for what reaches the customer, while still logging/keeping `e.rawMessage` + `registrarId` server-side (e.g. in whatever audit-log/console-error mechanism that call site already uses — don't invent a new logging path, use what's already there). Also fix:
- `lib/actions-domains.ts`'s "(name.com API keys missing)" string → registrar-neutral ("domain registration is not configured yet").
- `setWhoisPrivacy`'s note → drop the `${domain.registrar}` interpolation entirely; it doesn't need to name anything to be informative.
- `lib/kb-tools.ts`'s `describeService()` → remove the `Registrar: ${domain.registrar}` line from the AI context entirely (no product value, pure risk — don't replace it with anything, just delete that line).

## Standing rules for this repo (non-negotiable)

- Any Prisma schema change must be written as a migration file for human review — you must NEVER run `prisma migrate deploy`/`db push` or apply one yourself. This task shouldn't need any schema change; if you find yourself wanting one, stop and flag it instead.
- Never rotate, regenerate, or touch any live credential on any real infrastructure.
- Match the codebase's existing comment style: comments explain non-obvious WHY, not WHAT. Don't over-comment.
- Don't touch anything related to Phase 1's already-shipped consolidation logic beyond adding the `RegistrarError` class and having existing functions throw it instead of a plain `Error` — the actual HTTP call shapes (method/path/body) must not change at all.

## Verification (required before reporting done)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full test suite (`npm test`), diffed by exact failing-test-name against a fresh run on `main` in the same worktree — zero NEW failures, plus your new leak-guard test and any new tests for `RegistrarError`'s message-mapping passing.
3. Confirm the leak-guard test genuinely catches a regression: temporarily reintroduce one of the original leaks in a scratch copy (or just verify logically that the test's grep pattern would have failed against the pre-fix code you already have in git history) — don't leave any temporary/reverted test state committed, this is just a sanity check on the test's own effectiveness.
4. Commit your work on the `feature/registrar-leak-fixes` branch inside the worktree (do not push, do not merge to main, do not deploy anywhere — needs review before it goes anywhere near staging/production).

Report back with: the exact list of files changed and what changed in each, the final wording you chose for each of the 4 static-copy fixes (so it can be reviewed for tone), the `RegistrarError` customer-message categories you implemented, confirmation of tsc/test results, and anything you found that didn't match the audit as described (a leak already fixed, a new one you found, wording you're unsure about).

1	# Multi-registrar domain sourcing (name.com + Namecheap + Enom)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Nxeon sells domains through exactly one registrar today (name.com), via a reseller API. The owner wants to add Namecheap and Enom as additional backends so that every domain search/purchase automatically uses whichever registrar is cheapest after Nxeon's markup — maximizing margin and/or offering customers the best price — while the registrar's identity stays completely invisible to customers (search results, error messages, DNS/nameserver copy, the AI chat assistant) and visible only in admin views, per-domain.
6	
7	This scope was built from a full audit of the existing registrar code and every customer-facing surface that currently names "name.com" directly. Two structural findings shape the whole plan:
8	
9	- **There are 3 separate hardcoded name.com HTTP clients today**, not one: `lib/registrar.ts` (the main one), plus private duplicates inside `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (nameservers/WHOIS/outbound-transfer) and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (URL forwarding/registrar lock). Designing a multi-registrar interface against 3 different existing shapes at once is how it ends up wrong in three different ways — they must be consolidated into one `NameComRegistrar` implementation FIRST, as a pure no-behavior-change refactor, before any second registrar is added.
10	- **The registrar decision must freeze at the same moment as the price it's paired with.** `purchaseDomain`'s direct-wallet path re-quotes fresh right before charging; its card path freezes `{priceCents, costCents}` into a `DomainOrderIntent` row at Stripe-session-creation time and never re-quotes at fulfillment. Once multiple registrars exist, "cheapest registrar" is part of that same frozen quote — `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` need a `registrar` field alongside `priceCents`/`costCents`, not a separate re-decision step later. Getting this wrong means a card order quoted against one registrar could silently try to fulfill through a different (by-then-cheaper) one, which has no record of that domain — invisible to the customer, but a real operational bug.
11	
12	Also found: `Domain.registrar` (`prisma/schema.prisma`) already has `@default("namecheap")` even though every write site hardcodes the literal `"name.com"` — a landmine nobody has hit yet only because every create site sets it explicitly. Fix this default as part of the schema work.
13	
14	## Confirmed customer-facing registrar-identity leaks (must be closed as part of this work)
15	
16	1. `app/dashboard/domains/page.tsx:83` — nameserver label literally "Default (name.com)".

25	## Approach
26	
27	### Phase 1 — Consolidate the 3 name.com clients into one `NameComRegistrar`
28	
29	Pure refactor, zero behavior change, ships to production on its own before any second registrar exists. Move every name.com call currently duplicated in `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (`updateNameservers`, `setWhoisPrivacy`, `requestTransferOut`'s unlock/getAuthCode) and `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock) into `lib/registrar.ts` as new exported functions. Delete both files' private `nc()`/`baseUrl()`/`authHeader()` clones; both call sites import the consolidated exports instead. This collapses 3 separate `` `name.com: ${msg}` `` error-formatting sites down to 1, which Phase 5 depends on. Verify with `npm test` plus a full staging smoke pass (nameserver update, WHOIS toggle, transfer-out unlock, URL forwarding CRUD, registrar lock toggle) before touching anything else.
30	
31	### Phase 2 — The `RegistrarClient` abstraction
32	
33	New `lib/registrars/types.ts` defines the interface covering everything a registrar does today: `checkDomains`, `registerDomain`, `renewDomain`, `domainInfo`, `disableRegistrarAutorenew`, the inbound-transfer lifecycle (`checkTransfer`/`createTransfer`/`getTransfer`/`cancelTransfer`/`listTransfers`), DNS CRUD (`listRecords`/`addRecord`/`deleteRecord`/`getDnsHosts`), and the Phase-1-consolidated nameserver/WHOIS/lock/forwarding functions. Each implementation also exposes `id` ("namecom"/"namecheap"/"enom", the DB/dispatch value) and `label` ("name.com"/"Namecheap"/"eNom", admin-display-only — never passed to a customer-facing function). `transferOutcome`/`transferStatusLabel` and `domainMarkupPct`/`retailCents` stay free, registrar-agnostic functions — status bucketing and markup are platform concepts, not per-registrar behavior.
34	
35	`lib/registrars/index.ts` exports `ALL_REGISTRARS`, `configuredRegistrars()` (env-configured AND admin-enabled, see Phase 7), and `registrarById(id)`.
36	
37	**Dispatch rule**: for a domain that already has a DB row, every call site resolves `registrarById(domain.registrar)` and calls through that — critical because a domain fulfilled through Namecheap has no record at name.com, so it must never silently fail over to a different backend even if that backend later gets disabled for new business. For a new search/quote (no DB row yet) or a new inbound-transfer quote, fan out to `configuredRegistrars()` instead (Phase 3).
38	
39	### Phase 3 — Price-shopping mechanism
40	
41	`lib/tools/domain-availability.ts`'s `checkAvailabilityBatched()` (the shared cache/batch/rate-limit wrapper used by both the marketing domain checker and the signed-in wizard) becomes a fan-out: each configured registrar keeps its own cache entries (key becomes `(registrarId, domain)`, since two registrars quoting the same domain are two different facts), its own batch size (name.com's verified 24/call does not necessarily apply to Namecheap/Enom — must be verified per-registrar against real endpoints), and its own rate-limit bucket (`` `registrar:availability:${registrarId}:global` ``, so one registrar's outage/slowness can't throttle the others). Merge step: for each domain, pick the lowest `priceCents` among registrars reporting `available: true`; treat a domain as "taken" only if at least one registrar explicitly says so; if every registrar returns `unknown`, the merged result is `unknown`, never a fabricated status. The customer-facing `DomainResult` type never carries a registrar id — that only exists in an internal-only return path used by `purchaseDomain`'s pre-charge re-quote and the eventual `Domain.registrar` write, so registrar identity is kept out of the client bundle by construction, not convention.
42	
43	The purchase-time re-check (`checkDomains([domain])`, currently called fresh right before charging) becomes `quoteCheapest(domain)`, fanning out to all configured registrars with no cache (this is deliberately the anti-staleness check), returning the winning `{registrar, check}`. `DomainOrderPrice`/`DomainOrderIntent` gain a `registrar` field so the card-payment path's frozen quote and the eventual `registerDomain`/`disableRegistrarAutorenew` calls agree on which backend to use.
44	
45	**Markup stays a single global percentage** (`domainMarkupPct()`, unchanged) applied uniformly to whichever registrar's cost wins — this keeps "cheapest cost," "cheapest retail," and "best margin for Nxeon" all pointing at the same registrar automatically, avoiding a three-way tradeoff. Per-registrar differential markup is an explicit non-goal unless requested separately.
46	
47	### Phase 4 — Real Namecheap/Enom integration work (owner action items called out plainly)
48	
49	I have not verified current 2026 account-approval terms, minimum-balance requirements, or sandbox capabilities for either registrar — these change and are gated behind an application process, so they need to be checked directly against each registrar's live reseller documentation before committing to a timeline:
50	
51	- **Namecheap**: historically account-age/spend-gated API access (not a separate paid tier), IP-allowlisted auth (Nxeon's production egress IP must be registered and kept in sync), XML-based responses via query-string GET commands (`namecheap.domains.check`, `.create`, `.renew`, `.dns.setHosts`, `.transfer.create`) — needs an XML parser (`fast-xml-parser` is already a dependency), unlike name.com's plain JSON REST. Has historically offered a sandbox (`api.sandbox.namecheap.com`) — confirm whether registration actually completes there or only availability checks work.
52	- **Enom**: Tucows-owned (same parent as name.com), historically a more traditional paid reseller program — do not assume it mirrors name.com's terms. Auth via username + API password over query-string GET; response format historically XML with a newer JSON option — confirm current default. Its test-environment story is the least documented of the three; budget real discovery time here, since its absence would mean `EnomRegistrar` can only be verified against small real production transactions.
53	
54	Each new registrar gets its own `lib/registrars/namecheap.ts` / `lib/registrars/enom.ts` with its own private HTTP helper — there's no meaningful shared transport code across three structurally different APIs; the Phase-1 consolidation win is entirely about eliminating name.com's *own* triplication.
55	
56	### Phase 5 — Closing the leak surface
57	
58	**Static UI copy** (leaks #1–4): one constant module (e.g. `lib/registrar-copy.ts`) exporting neutral labels ("our registrar partner" / generic DNS copy — exact wording is a product call, see Open Questions), used at each of the 4 file locations instead of the literal string. Add a standing test (`test/*.test.ts`, this repo's existing pattern) that greps `components/customer/**` and `app/dashboard/**` for `"name.com"`/`"namecheap"`/`"enom"` and fails if found outside an admin allowlist — turns this from a one-time fix into an enforced invariant, which matters more with 3 registrars than 1.
59	
60	**Dynamic leaks** (#5–8, the structural fix): introduce a `RegistrarError` class at the `RegistrarClient` HTTP-helper boundary carrying `{registrarId, rawMessage, customerMessage}` — `customerMessage` is a generic, pattern-matched, registrar-name-free string ("We couldn't complete this with our registrar right now — no charge was made, try again or contact support" for known failure categories, a generic fallback otherwise). Replace the page's single "Registrar: name.com" stat card and "via name.com" header copy with per-registrar configured/enabled status, since one value no longer describes the system.
63	
64	### Phase 6 — Data migration
65	
66	**None needed.** The one domain that ever completed a registration attempt was FAILED and has since been deleted — production has zero domain rows today. Just fix the schema's stray `@default("namecheap")` (drop the default entirely, or default to `"namecom"` matching current real behavior) as part of the Phase-2 schema change; no backfill script, no reclassification logic. Sanity-check with `SELECT count(*) FROM "Domain"` immediately before shipping the schema change, purely to confirm this hasn't changed.
67	
68	### Phase 7 — Staged rollout
69	
70	1. Ship Phase 1 (consolidation) alone, to production, first — isolates "did the refactor break name.com" from anything multi-registrar.
71	2. Add per-registrar admin kill-switches in `lib/settings.ts` (`registrar_namecom_enabled` default `"true"`, `registrar_namecheap_enabled`/`registrar_enom_enabled` default `"false"`), same pattern as the existing `kb_bot_enabled` flag. `configuredRegistrars()` checks both env-var presence and this setting.
72	3. Ship the `RegistrarClient` abstraction with Namecheap/Enom flags OFF — behaviorally identical to today, isolating "did the abstraction regress name.com" from "does a new registrar work."
73	4. Enable Namecheap in staging once credentials exist; run the full lifecycle (search, register, renew, DNS, nameservers, WHOIS, outbound transfer, inbound transfer quote/submit/poll/cancel) before flipping it on in production. Repeat independently for Enom — never enable both for the first time simultaneously, so a bad merge (e.g. a malformed response corrupting the cheapest-price pick) has a precise, single kill-switch to hit.
74	5. No new monitoring primitive needed — `registerDomainCore`'s existing `verifyRegistration`/needs-review machinery already handles ambiguous registrar failures per-domain once dispatch goes through `registrarById(domain.registrar)`; just confirm admin's needs-review/FAILED views also show the new Registrar column so ops can tell which backend is failing.
75	6. Land the Phase-5 leak-guard test in CI so it runs on every future PR, not just once at launch — a manual QA pass won't catch a leak introduced months later by an unrelated feature.
76	
77	## Open questions for the owner (not blocking the plan, but blocking Phase 4+ timeline)
78	
79	1. **Namecheap/Enom account approval, minimum balance, and sandbox capability** — needs verifying directly against each registrar's current reseller program; I can't confirm 2026 terms from here. If either lacks a real registration sandbox, staging verification for that registrar's purchase path may not be possible pre-production.
80	2. **Exact neutral copy** for the "our registrar partner"-style UI strings (Phase 5) — a wording preference, not a technical decision.
81	3. **What the customer sees, if anything, about multi-sourcing** — recommend the search results page stays byte-for-byte identical to today (say nothing about multiple providers), since the requirement is registrar identity must be invisible; confirm this is the intent versus wanting a subtle "we shop multiple providers" trust signal.
82	4. **Registrars disagreeing on availability** (registry sync lag) — recommend: available if any configured registrar says available with a price; taken only if none do; log disagreements for ops. This is a customer-trust/messaging call worth the owner's sign-off, not just an engineering default.
